Title: Freshing up my memory on contesting

Messages.Author: Oortje
Messages.Body:
This might be nitpicking, but help me out.

situation 1
Player a has anson with an ivory bow
player b plays anson and they start contesting.
play b plays an ivory bow on a igo.
Is the ivory bow contested?

situation 2
Player a has anson with ivory bow
Player b plays an ivory bow on igo and starts contesting
Player b plays anson and starts contesting anson
Is the ivory bow still contested?

If yes. The situation continues.
Player b yields contesting on igo. And plays a new ivory bow on igo. Is that one contested?

situation 3
Player a has anson with ivory bow. Anson gets banished.
PLayer b plays anson with ivory bow.
Player a transfers out anson (still with bow)
Is the bow contested?

Thanks in advance.

Have a cold long night,
Jeroen van Oort
Dutch National Coördinator

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
It's all in the rulebook:

> Non-existant user wrote:
> Some of the cards in the game represent unique resources, such as specific locations, equipment or people. These cards will be identified as "unique" in their card text. In addition, all crypt cards represent unique minions. If more than one unique card with the same name is brought into play, that means control of the card is being contested. For the duration of the contest, all of the contested cards are turned face down and are out of play. If another unique card with the same name is brought into play, it is immediately contested and turned face down as well.
>
The only thing that matters is: is the card already in play (contested or not)? Being on another contested card doesn't change anything.

So
1/ Both Ivory Bow and Anson are contested
2/ Both Ivory Bow and Anson are contested
2'/ Ivory Bow has been yielded. A new Ivory Bow comes in play. There's already one in play, so it becomes contested.
3/ Both Ivory Bow and Anson are contested

Messages.Author: Juggernaut1981
Messages.Body:
> Borrelstein wrote:
> So that implies that equipment and other cards on a contested vampire remain in play during the contest, and can be destroyed/stolen etc? Good to know!
>
Nope, the incoming Unique card checks if any player has one under contest or in play, and then responds.

So Igo has an Ivory Bow.
Igo gets contested, so his Ivory Bow "vanishes" into the contest.
Anson gets an Ivory Bow, but Anson's Ivory bow knows that Igo has an Ivory Bow. So Anson's Ivory Bow contests Igo's Ivory Bow.

While they are being contested other cards cannot target them because they are not in play. It is the same story as when cards "know" you've played that card this Turn/Game/Action (i.e. Cancelling Immortal Grapple).

Retired Baron of Sydney, Australia, 418

Messages.Author: Borrelstein
Messages.Body: Well I know that the contested cards are out of play, but how about the non-contested cards like equipment or The Rack placed on a contested vamp?

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Borrelstein wrote:
> Well I know that the contested cards are out of play, but how about the non-contested cards like equipment
>
Equipment is put on the vampire, so it's out of play while the vampire is contested.

> Borrelstein wrote:
> or The Rack placed on a contested vamp?
>
The Rack isn't "placed on" a vampire. It is put in play, and targets a vampire. If that vampire is contested, the Rack stays in play and doesn't give blood until the vampire returns in play or stolen.
